policy.discovery: hermes skills search <query> — confirm a skill exists before installing it
policy.inspect: hermes skills inspect <skill> — read what it does before installing
policy.verify: hermes -p <profile> skills list — record the inventory after install
policy.builtin_first: Every profile ships ~57 builtin skills enabled by default (test-driven-development, systematic-debugging, github, codebase-inspection, computer-use, google-workspace, arxiv...). Run hermes -p <profile> skills list first — a builtin covering the role's need satisfies it; search the Hub only for genuine gaps and never install a duplicate of an enabled builtin.

security_gate.rule: Scan any skill from OUTSIDE the official HERMES Skills Hub (third-party repos, direct URLs) before install. On any risk finding: skip, report, never install from that source. Official Hub skills are exempt.

policy.never: Never invent skill names. A rejected name means stop — not retry with new guesses.

trusted_packs.name: superpowers
trusted_packs.note: Agentic dev methodology pack (TDD, debugging, planning, collaboration patterns). Scan with SkillSpector and adapt to HERMES skill format before install.
trusted_packs.verification: unverified-in-hub — run hermes skills search superpowers first; if not on the Hub, treat as third-party and gate it

rule: This manifest provides search terms and vetted third-party packs — never final skill names. The provisioning agent checks the profile's enabled builtins first, then confirms genuine gaps at runtime with hermes skills search, installs, and reports coverage per profile.
